subject: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request

Team,

Customer ask (FinHealth) landed during yesterday's call: they need a way to mark specific tenants/datasets as retention-exempt (legal hold / preservation), plus an admin flow to manage those exemptions scoped by geography. High-level asks from the customer:
- Per-tenant "exemption" flag that prevents automatic deletion/purge even if standard TTL applies.
- Ability to tie exemptions to region placement (e.g., ensure payment artifacts for tenant X are stored physically in eu-west1).
- Admin UI for Compliance/SecOps to add/remove exemptions and view an audit trail.
- API equivalents for automation + audit log entries that are immutable for 5 years.
- Exportable report (CSV) listing all active exemptions and their metadata.

I've attached a workbook from FinHealth with specific rows they expect us to surface (finhealth-data-residency-reqs.xlsx) and a sketch from Solutions (retention-exemptions-spec-v1.pdf).

Asking Product + Eng: can we get a rough implementation scope and timeline to present to the customer next Tuesday? Ideally a prototype/demo in Q3 (12 weeks) and GA-ish in Q4, but I want your realistic engineering input. Specific questions:
1) What are the DB/model changes needed to record exemption state + region binding?
2) Effort to add an admin UI page + RBAC to manage exemptions?
3) Audit log durability and retention implications (S3/GCS buckets vs internal DB)?
4) Any blockers for physically pinning storage to a region vs tagging metadata only?

Please reply with blockers/assumptions and a rough RAG timeline. If this requires legal sign-off or an architecture review board, flag it.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finhealth-data-residency-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet), retention-exemptions-spec-v1.pdf (sketch)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request

Marissa — thanks for the write-up. A few clarifying questions before I scope work: 

On Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Customer ask (FinHealth) landed during yesterday's call: they need a way to mark specific tenants/datasets as retention-exempt (legal hold / preservation), plus an admin flow to manage those exemptions scoped by geography.

Questions/notes from Eng perspective:
- Scale: do we have an approximate count of tenants/customers that will need exemptions (one-off vs many)? This affects metadata indexing and query patterns.
- Model: I assume we add a tenant_retention_policy table that references tenant_id -> {default_ttl, exemption_flag, region_constraint, created_by, created_at}. Is that OK for Product?
- Admin UI vs API parity: customer wants UI + API. Building the UI isn't the heavy lift; syncing RBAC and audit immutability is.
- Storage placement: tagging objects with region metadata is cheap; guaranteeing physical-only-in-region (non-replicated) is more invasive (requires storage zone routing and replication controls). Which does FinHealth actually mean?
- Legal hold semantics: is exemption a strict "no-delete until cleared" (immutable) or a soft-preserve where writes are allowed but deletion requires a workflow? This changes snapshotting/archiving needs.

I'll wait for FinHealth to confirm counts and semantics. Tentatively: prototype API + DB changes 4–6 weeks, admin UI + RBAC + audit 8–10 weeks, storage placement work depends on infra (estimate +4–8 weeks if we need non-replicated regional placement).

-karthik

From: Samir Patel <samir@finhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@finhealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick follow-up. A few clarifications from our side to help scope:
- Expected scope: ~12 active production tenants that will need long-term exemptions; ~7 of these will have formal legal holds for ongoing litigation/regulatory reviews.
- Legal hold semantics: for those 7 tenants we require an immutable-preservation state — no deletes, full-content retention, and a tamper-evident audit record. For the remaining tenants an "exemption" that prevents auto-ttl deletion is acceptable.
- Regional placement: payments and banking logs for EU customers MUST reside in EU physical infrastructure (eu-west1). We cannot accept logical tags alone for those artifacts — must be physically stored in-region.
- Audit: logs of exemption changes and erasure attempts must be retained for 5 years and available as export.
- API: yes, we need an API to script onboarding and bulk exemption changes. UI is preferred for day-to-day ops.

I've attached a spreadsheet with row-level examples and our compliance team's notes (finhealth-data-residency-reqs.xlsx). We're on a procurement timeline — need a clear feasibility and ETA before next Wednesday (2027-05-06).

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Ops
FinHealth Inc.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request

Marissa / team — digesting Samir's note. Answering Karthik's and adding feasibility & risk notes.

On Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 11:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for the write-up. A few clarifying questions before I scope work: 

Feasibility summary:
- Metadata/model: implement tenant_retention_policy as Karthik suggested. Add audit_events table for immutability with WAL-style append-only semantics (immutable records; soft-delete only via append). Low risk.
- Admin UI + RBAC: straightforward; we can reuse the existing admin scaffold. Estimate 3 engineers for 6 weeks for UI + API endpoints and RBAC wiring.
- Physical region pinning: moderate-to-high effort. Our storage fabric currently replicates by default; allowing non-replicated, single-region buckets requires infra changes: zone affinity, replication policy flags, and S3/GCS bucket-level enforcement. This is the main gating item. Estimate +6–10 weeks of infra work and coordination with SRE.
- Audit durability: recommend writing audit proofs to an immutable object store (write-once GCS bucket with object lock) and a separate export index for quick queries. This affects cost and retention lifecycle.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior should remain current TTL flow; exemptions opt-in per tenant. We'll add migration jobs for existing tenants if the customer requests.

Proposed timeline (rough):
- Week 0–2: detailed spec & architecture review (write RFC + SRE review).
- Week 3–8: DB + API + audit pipeline prototype (internal).
- Week 6–12: Admin UI + RBAC + export CSV feature.
- Week 10–20: Storage-region pinning (parallel SRE project) — depends on infra calendar.

Blockers/asks:
- Legal/Compliance: exact immutability SLA and evidence format.
- SRE: timeline for storage replication change; is single-region enforcement allowed for the customer's chosen cloud region?
- Product: prioritize whether UI parity or storage enforcement is higher priority for initial release.

If Product wants, I can scope a minimal "exemption + UI + audit" MVP that keeps logical tags but defers physical pinning to a follow-up. That would reduce initial delivery to ~10–12 weeks.

-soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finhealth.com>, security@finhealth.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo retention exemptions & admin flow — roadmap request

Thanks, everyone — good set of feedback. Summarizing plan & owners so we can get FinHealth a single ETA and move procurement forward: 

Action items / owners / target dates:
- Product (Marissa): finalize customer-facing requirements doc and confirm required fields with FinHealth (TODAY 2027-05-04 EOD).
- Eng (Karthik): draft DB schema + API contract (RFC) by 2027-05-11.
- Eng (Soojín): prototype audit pipeline and append-only audit storage proposal by 2027-05-18.
- Infra/SRE (Ben): feasibility check for single-region storage and rough effort estimate by 2027-05-21.
- Legal/Compliance (Irene): advise on immutability evidence format and retention obligations by 2027-05-14.

Proposed delivery options to offer FinHealth:
A) MVP (recommended for procurement): exemption flag + API + Admin UI + append-only audit (logical tagging only) — target ~12 weeks (demo to customer).
B) Full compliance path: MVP + single-region physical pinning + hardened object-lock audit stores — target 20+ weeks (depends on infra calendar).

Samir: please confirm whether MVP (A) suffices for procurement or whether you need the full compliance path (B) signed in the SOW. If you can confirm earlier today, we'll prioritize accordingly.

I'll upload the finalized requirements doc and the action tracker to Confluence after Irene's legal notes.

Best,
Marissa
